concerns.text: Task T024b reduces the sample size (effective_N) based on runtime constraints BEFORE T025 measures convergence. SC-002 requires measuring convergence against 'N_valid' (participants passing motion QC). By shrinking the denominator before measurement, T024b makes it impossible to verify the ≥90% convergence rate against the true N_valid defined in the spec, violating SC-002.

FR-006 and SC-005 require a sensitivity analysis sweeping the 'belief-updating threshold/cutoff' (an input model parameter). Task T036a implements a sweep over 'alpha parameter values' (the output estimates). This tests stability of the output against itself rather than the robustness of the correlation rate against the input threshold, failing to satisfy FR-006.

SC-001 requires measuring the exclusion rate against the 10% motion threshold. Task T018b (which generates the required `data/reports/qc_summary.json` for this verification) is marked as incomplete `[ ]`. Without this task, the success criterion for the data pipeline is unverified, and downstream tasks may process excluded participants.

The plan specifies a target N=30, but SC-002 defines success as convergence ≥90% of 'N_valid' (dynamic count after QC). T024b logic reduces N based on runtime, creating a conflict where the 'effective_N' used for modeling may not align with the 'N_valid' required for the SC-002 calculation, potentially masking convergence failures.
